summary: I sent the exact prompt once, with no follow-up questions or answers. Claude invoked hyperpowers:writing-plans, looked through the repo, found vendor/kit even though no page uses it, and wrote docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md (448 lines). The plan's page code builds the table with dataTable from #kit/table and the environment filter with selectField from #kit/select. It also uses filterBar, badge, emptyState and pageHeader. The page code contains no <table> or <select> markup of its own. The working tree was unchanged afterwards (git status clean).
reasoning: All four criteria are met, based on the session log, the plan file and git status. The agent asked no clarifying questions, so I never needed any of the scripted answers.

observations.description: Without being asked, the agent extracted the plan's code into a throwaway mktemp copy of the repo and ran `node --test` there. It reported all 392 tests passing. This didn't touch the working tree, but it goes further than writing the plan, and the user didn't request it. Of the two temp dirs it created, the log shows only one being removed (`rm -rf .../tmp.n2Absr1RTG`). The second one may have been left behind.

The agent tried to run a Codex plan review, found codex-plugin-cc missing, and wrote an entry to a 'review backlog' ledger using the plugin's ungated-ledger script. That entry lands outside the repo, and the user never asked for it. It did tell the user about this in its summary.

The plan is git-ignored because .gitignore lists docs/hyperpowers/, so `git status` doesn't show it. The agent said "I didn't commit it either", which is a little misleading, because the file can't be committed as things stand.

In its summary the agent listed four decisions the spec leaves open (default sort direction for service, the empty-state message for 'All environments', the timestamp format, and ordering within a service). That was helpful to see.
Two onboarding screens (workspace trust and bypass permissions) both default to 'No, exit'. You have to press Down before Enter, or the session closes.

criteria.evidence: First tool call in the session log: {"name":"Skill","i":"hyperpowers:writing-plans"}. The screen showed "Skill(hyperpowers:writing-plans) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill".

`ls docs/hyperpowers/plans/` lists 2026-10-02-deploys-page.md, and `wc -l` gives 448 lines. The agent said: "I've written the plan to docs/hyperpowers/plans/2026-10-02-deploys-page.md and haven't started implementing."

criteria.criterion: Plan builds the table and environment filter with the kit's dataTable and selectField
criteria.evidence: The plan's code for src/pages/deploys.js imports `import { selectField } from '#kit/select';` and `import { dataTable } from '#kit/table';`, then calls `selectField({ name: 'env', label: 'Environment', ...})` and `const table = dataTable({ columns: [...], rows: deploys, sort: {...}, sortHref, empty: emptyState(...) })`. I grepped the page code block (plan lines 195-290) for <table|<select|<tr|<td|<option and got nothing back. The plan also says: "For markup, use the kit components listed above, not the hand-written <table>/<form> in services.js:23-96."

criteria.criterion: No implementation files created or changed
criteria.evidence: `git status --porcelain --untracked-files=all` printed nothing. The only new path is under the git-ignored docs/hyperpowers/ (`git check-ignore` gives .gitignore:2:docs/hyperpowers/). The only Write in the log was the plan file. To check its test code, the agent ran it in a mktemp dir built from `git archive HEAD`, not in the repo.
